Transworld Good Wood 2018 review: Testers described the Propaganda as "balanced" and "easy-going" [38] 127. Transworld review – strengths: "Soft and predictable flex pattern for technical rail moves" and "easy manipulation" [38] 128. Transworld review – weakness: "The trait some testers felt this board lacked was stability—a tradeoff for its relaxed persona" [38] 129. Transworld review – pressing ability: "exceptional pressing ability" — "It's super malleable but has enough beneath you that it's reassuring" [38] 130. Transworld review – best use case: "More comfortable navigating triple kinks than sending 80-footers" [38] 131. Tactics review (2020): "If you're looking for a budget-friendly park board that features top of the line construction, look no further" [39] 132. Tactics review – ride feel: "Playful when you want it and precise when you need it" [39] 133. BoardParadise retailer assessment: "Park Rats and slashers rejoice the price and performance" [40] 134. BoardParadise assessment: "Simplistic graphics and artwork accompanied by unrivaled tech" [40] 135. Whitelines 2010/11 review: Propaganda described as "For fullgrown jib enthusiasts" [41] 136. The-House review (2021, older camber model): Noted sandwich construction, aspen and poplar core with carbon fibre stringers, biax fiberglass [42] — NOTE: This review was of an older model that had a camber profile, extruded base, and was made in Austria. The current 2025 model differs significantly (Zero Camber, sintered base, made in USA). --- HISTORICAL NOTES / MODEL EVOLUTION --- 137. Prior manufacturing location: Older Propaganda models (pre-~2020) were made in Austria [42] 138. Current manufacturing location: USA (Never Summer Factory, Denver) [10][11] 139. Previous base type (older models): Extruded 2000 base [42] 140. Current base type: Sintered 4501 base [19] 141. Previous core (older models): Aspen and poplar with carbon fibre stringers [42] 142. Current core: Canadian aspen Ultralight Core [19] 143. Prior Propaganda (2010/11) flex rating: 5 out of 10 [41] 144. Current flex rating: 6.5 out of 10 [1][19] 145. Academy brand first year: 2002 [2] — the Propaganda model has existed since at least 2010/11 [41] 146. Limited edition variant: Propaganda Cookies SF Collab Limited Snowboard 2024 [28] --- COMPARABLE/COMPETITOR PRODUCTS --- 147. Academy Propacamba: Same brand, Micro Camber version (cambered Propaganda sibling), Transworld Good Wood 2019 Men's Park Winner [43][44] 148. Nitro T1: Zero Camber twin park board, medium flex — direct competitor in flat profile category [45] 149. Burton Name Dropper: Flat Top profile, asymmetric twin — another flat park competitor [45] 150. Salomon Huck Knife: Rock Out Camber, twin shape, medium flex — popular park alternative [46] 151. CAPiTA DOA (Defenders of Awesome): Camber dominant true twin, Good Wood award winner — common competitor in the park category [17] 152. Ride Warpig: Another Good Wood park winner in the same year as Propaganda [17] 153. GNU Headspace: Good Wood park winner 2018 — alternative park board [17] 154. Lib Tech Box Knife: Good Wood park winner 2018 — alternative park board [17] 155. Bataleon Evil Twin: True twin with 3BT, camber between feet, biax fiberglass — park-focused alternative [47] --- KEY DECISION FACTORS / RIDE CHARACTERISTICS --- 156. Riding style focus: Primarily jibbing (boxes, rails, tubes) with all-mountain versatility [19] 157. Target rider: Park riders from beginners to highly advanced jibbers [30] 158. Gender target: Men's snowboard [30] 159. Forgivingness: Described as "super forgiving and easy to ride" by manufacturer and multiple reviewers [19][30] 160. Pop: Good pop noted despite flat camber profile [24][38] 161. Buttering: Excellent for buttering and pressing — highlighted by multiple reviewers [24][38] 162. Edge hold: Enhanced by Vario Power Grip Sidecut — "hold an edge better than most flat profile boards" [24] 163. Speed stability: Underfoot Balancing Stabilisers add high-speed stability [19] 164. Vibration damping: Featherweight Damping System plus rubber dampening for chatter-free carving [19][30] 165. Switch riding: True twin design makes switch riding natural [19] 166. Value proposition: Described as "cost effective" by manufacturer [19] 167. Construction durability: Built at Never Summer factory — "built like a tank" per user review of Academy boards [37] 168. Flat camber trade-off: Less stable at high speed and less pop than full camber boards — a general characteristic of flat profiles [45][48] 169. Boot size limitation: 152cm waist width (244mm) may be too narrow for boots size 9-10 US [24] 170. Sintered base maintenance: Requires more frequent waxing than extruded bases but provides faster performance [30] 171. Base speed: Fast sintered base praised by multiple reviewers [19][36] 172. Construction: USA-made at Never Summer provides quality comparable to Never Summer's own boards [37][14] 173. Small brand customer service: Multiple users praise personalized service, stickers, thank-you notes [24][37] 174. Brand social following: Relatively small/niche brand with ~24K Instagram followers [15] — compared to major brands like Burton or CAPiTA 175. Limited distribution: Limited international dealer network — a user from Japan wished for more distributors [24]
